original_interpretation: Amkor's top-10 customers were 72% of 2025 net sales; Apple 29.8%, Qualcomm 11.1% (direct sales).
evidence_found: "Our ten largest customers accounted for 72% of our net sales in 2025. Direct sales to Apple and Qualcomm accounted for 29.8% and 11.1% of our net sales, respectively, for the year ended December 31, 2025." (2025 Form 10-K, Item 1, Customers)
notes: Opened via SEC EDGAR (declared user agent). Figures are direct sales only; sales via other channels to these end customers not counted.

original_interpretation: ASE 2025 net revenues NT$645,388m, +8.4%.
evidence_found: "Net revenues for the full year of 2025 amounted to NT$645,388 million, up by 8.4% from the full year of 2024." (FY2025 results release). 20-F: "Operating revenues increased by 8.4% to NT$645,387.7 million (US$20,573.4 million) in 2025" (Item 5).
notes: Unaudited release figure matches the audited 20-F filed 2026-04-01. SRC-0093 is a PR Newswire copy of ASE's own release; company_documentation is acceptable.

original_interpretation: ASE 2025 consolidated gross margin 17.7%; ATM gross margin 23.5%.
evidence_found: Consolidated: "Gross margin increased by 1.4 percentage points to 17.7% in 2025 from 16.3% in 2024." ATM section: "Gross margin increased to 23.5% in 2025 from 22.5% in 2024." (FY2025 results release). 20-F Item 5: "gross margin, was 17.7% in 2025 compared to 16.3% in 2024".
notes: Release defines ATM as 'semiconductor assembly and testing services'; the claim's 'assembly, testing and materials' expansion is the common reading but is not spelled out in this release.

original_interpretation: ASE 2025 equipment capex US$3,396m (2,104 packaging, 1,140 testing, 139 EMS).
evidence_found: "Equipment capital expenditures in 2025 totaled US$3,396 million, of which US$2,104 million was used in packaging operations, US$1,140 million in testing operations, US$139 million in EMS operations and US$13 million in interconnect materials operations and others." (FY2025 results release, Liquidity)
correction: Breakdown omits US$13 million for interconnect materials and others; components sum to 3,396 only with it.

original_interpretation: Packaging ~48%, testing ~11%, EMS ~40% of ASE 2025 revenue.
evidence_found: "Net revenues from packaging operations, testing operations, EMS operations and others represented approximately 48%, 11%, 40% and 1% of total net revenues for the year, respectively." (FY2025 results release, Full-Year Highlights – Consolidated)
notes: Note: the same release coincidentally reports raw material cost at 48% and labor at 11% of revenue; do not confuse.

original_interpretation: GF has multiple LTAs: customer commitments in exchange for GF capacity reservations.
evidence_found: "We have entered into multiple LTAs that provide for significant customer commitments in return for capacity reservation commitments from us." (2025 Form 20-F, Item 3.D Risk Factors)
notes: Opened via SEC EDGAR.

original_interpretation: If GF misses capacity reservation commitments it may owe substantial cash penalties.
evidence_found: "If we're unable to meet the capacity reservation commitments, we face the risk of defaulting on our obligations to our customers, which could result in us owing substantial cash penalties to our customers." (2025 Form 20-F, Item 3.D)
notes: Risk-factor language: a possibility, not a reported event.

original_interpretation: Some GF LTAs now have longer commitment periods for the same volume.
evidence_found: "We have renegotiated a number of LTAs with certain of our customers, including in 2025, as a result of which some of our LTAs now have longer commitment periods over which the customer may purchase the same volume as originally negotiated, and some of our LTAs have lower pricing or volume commitments than originally negotiated." (2025 Form 20-F, Item 3.D)
notes: Source supports the researcher's note: 'some customers under LTAs have requested to adjust their demand outlook downward and have sought renegotiation'. Fuller context (lower pricing/volume in some LTAs) added as a new claim.

original_interpretation: Nov 2024 GF–Commerce CHIPS direct funding agreement for up to US$1.5bn.
evidence_found: "In November 2024, the Company entered into a direct funding agreement (the “Direct Funding Agreement”) with the U.S. Department of Commerce for up to $1.5 billion in planned direct funding of Company projects in Malta, New York, and Burlington, Vermont, under the CHIPS and Science Act." (2025 Form 20-F, Item 3.D)
correction: Accurate as of signing; in January 2025 a further US$75 million of proposed funding was added (advanced packaging/test centre at Fab 8), so the agreement now totals up to about US$1.575bn (new claim in this batch).
notes: Funding is milestone-based; 20-F: 'In 2025, we received funding for the achievement of the first two milestones for the expansion of the Fab 8 facility.'

original_interpretation: In 2025 GF executed an agreement with New York State to secure US$570m.
evidence_found: "In 2025, the Company executed an agreement with the State of New York to secure $570 million to further support the Fab 8 projects (the “NY Agreement”). Like the Direct Funding Agreement, the NY Agreement contains milestones to be achieved in order to receive funds" (2025 Form 20-F, Item 3.D)
notes: Milestone-conditional commitment, not cash received.

original_interpretation: GF 2025 revenue US$6.791bn.
evidence_found: "Key Full Year 2025 Financial Highlights •Revenue of $6.791 billion"; Summary Annual Results: "Net revenue | $ 6,791 | $ 6,750" (4Q25 release). 20-F: "Net revenue | $ 6,791 | $ 6,750".
notes: Preliminary release figure matches the 20-F.

original_interpretation: GF 2025 'GAAP' gross margin 24.9%.
evidence_found: "Gross margin of 24.9% and Non-IFRS gross margin(1) of 26.1%" (4Q25 release, Key Full Year 2025 Financial Highlights); Summary Annual Results "Gross margin | 24.9 % | 24.5 %".
correction: Figure correct, but GlobalFoundries reports under IFRS, not US GAAP: it is the IFRS gross margin (non-IFRS 26.1%). Superseding claim added.

original_interpretation: GF shipped 2,345k 300mm-equivalent wafers in 2025, +10% from 2,124k.
evidence_found: Summary Annual Results: "Wafer shipments (300mm equivalent) (in thousands) | 2,345 | 2,124 | 221 | 10 %" (4Q25 release). 20-F: "higher wafer shipment volumes totaling 2.3 million (300mm equivalent), a 10.4% increase".

original_interpretation: Inference: GF 2025 revenue/wafer ≈ US$2,900, an upper bound on average wafer price.
evidence_found: Inputs verified: revenue 6,791 (CLM-0178) / 2,345k wafers (CLM-0180) = 2,896. 20-F end-market table: "Non wafer revenue 769" of total 6,791.
correction: Arithmetic and the 'upper bound' logic hold. A tighter figure is available: excluding US$769m non-wafer revenue (20-F), wafer revenue per wafer ≈ US$2,570 (new inference claim).
notes: Wafer revenue itself can include customer restructuring/underutilization payments (20-F), so even US$2,570 is not a pure ASP.

original_interpretation: GF 2025 purchases of PP&E and intangibles US$722m; government grant proceeds US$148m.
evidence_found: "Less: Purchases of property, plant and equipment and intangible assets ... (722)"; "Add: Proceeds from government grants ... 148"; "Total capital expenditures net of proceeds from government grants(1) ... (574)" (4Q25 release, Non-IFRS Adjusted Free Cash Flow reconciliation, year ended Dec 31, 2025)
notes: Figures are from the adjusted-FCF reconciliation table (not the full cash-flow statement as the evidence implied). Net capex after grants US$574m.

original_interpretation: Micron: past-5-year annual DRAM ASP changes ranged from ~+40% to ~-40% or worse.
evidence_found: "In the past five years, annual percentage changes in DRAM average selling prices have ranged from plus low 40% to a minus high 40% range." (FY2025 Form 10-K, Item 1A Risk Factors)
correction: The low end is 'minus high 40%' (i.e. roughly -45% to -49%), not 'about -40%'. Superseding claim with exact wording (and NAND range +low-30s to -low-50s) added.
notes: Latest 10-K available on 2026-10-01 (FY2026 10-K not yet filed).

original_interpretation: Micron LTAs: pricing, quantity and other terms periodically renegotiated.
evidence_found: "Due to volatile industry conditions, our customers are generally reluctant to enter into long-term, fixed-price purchase contracts. We typically enter into long-term agreements with our customers with acknowledgment that pricing, quantity, and other terms will be periodically negotiated to reflect market conditions and our customers' demand for our products." (FY2025 Form 10-K, Item 1)

original_interpretation: Micron FY2025 revenue US$37.38bn vs US$25.11bn FY2024.
evidence_found: "Fiscal 2025 highlights ... Revenue of $37.38 billion versus $25.11 billion for the prior year" (Q4 FY2025 release). Newer: FY2026 release (30 Sep 2026): "Revenue of $133.19 billion versus $37.38 billion for the prior year".
notes: Correct for FY2025, but no longer Micron's latest year: FY2026 (ended 3 Sep 2026) revenue was US$133.19bn (new claim). Do not present FY2025 as current.

original_interpretation: Micron FY2025 GAAP gross margin 39.8%.
evidence_found: Annual Financial Results: "Gross margin 14,873 ... percent of revenue 39.8 %" (GAAP FY-25) (Q4 FY2025 release). FY2026 release repeats FY-25 "39.8 %" and gives FY-26 "80.7 %".
notes: Correct for FY2025; FY2026 GAAP gross margin was 80.7% (new claim). Any cross-company margin comparison using 39.8% as Micron's current margin is stale.

original_interpretation: Micron FY2025 R&D US$3,798m.
evidence_found: Consolidated statements of operations, fiscal year: "Research and development ... 3,798 ... 3,430" (FY2025 | FY2024) (Q4 FY2025 release).
notes: FY2026 R&D was US$5,650m (new claim).

original_interpretation: Micron FY2025 PP&E expenditures US$15,857m; government incentive proceeds US$2,005m.
evidence_found: Cash flows from investing activities: "Expenditures for property, plant, and equipment (15,857)"; "Proceeds from government incentives 2,005" (Q4 FY2025 release).
notes: FY2026: US$30,712m and US$3,316m (new claim).

original_interpretation: Inference: Micron FY2025 gross capex ≈42% of revenue.
evidence_found: 15,857 / 37,378 = 42.4%; both inputs verified in the Q4 FY2025 release (CLM-0261, CLM-0264).
notes: Reasoning holds for FY2025. In FY2026 the ratio fell to about 23% (30,712 / 133,188) because revenue more than tripled (new inference claim); the 42% is cycle-specific, not structural.

original_interpretation: Aug 2025: US government to buy 433.3m Intel shares at US$20.47 (US$8.9bn, 9.9%), funded by US$5.7bn unpaid CHIPS grants + US$3.2bn Secure Enclave.
evidence_found: "the government agrees to purchase 433.3 million primary shares of Intel common stock at a price of $20.47 per share, equivalent to a 9.9 percent stake in the company." "funded by the remaining $5.7 billion in grants previously awarded, but not yet paid, to Intel under the U.S. CHIPS and Science Act and $3.2 billion awarded to the company as part of the Secure Enclave program." (8-K Ex. 99.1)
notes: Announcement terms. Closing mechanics (274.6m shares at closing, 158.7m escrowed for Secure Enclave, blended price) are covered by existing claims; the Q4 2025 release confirms escrowed shares still held at year-end.

original_interpretation: Five-year warrant at US$20/share for a further 5%, exercisable only if Intel's foundry ownership falls below 51%.
evidence_found: "The government will receive a five-year warrant, at $20 per share for an additional five percent of Intel common shares, exercisable only if Intel ceases to own at least 51% of the foundry business." (8-K Ex. 99.1)

original_interpretation: Intel 2025 revenue US$52.9bn, flat.

notes: Opened via curl of the intc.com-hosted 8-K exhibit (web_extract returned fragments only). Not adjusted for the Sept 2025 Altera deconsolidation.

original_interpretation: Intel 2025 GAAP gross margin 34.8%.
evidence_found: Full-Year 2025 table: "Gross margin | 34.8% | 32.7% | up 2.1 ppts" (GAAP 2025 | 2024); "GAAP gross margin percentage ... 34.8 %" (reconciliation).
notes: Non-GAAP 36.7%.

original_interpretation: Intel 2025 R&D US$13.8bn.
evidence_found: Income statement, twelve months: "Research and development | ... | 13,774 | 16,546" (2025 | 2024). Separately: "R&D and MG&A ($B) | $18.4 | $22.1".

original_interpretation: Intel 2025 gross capex US$17.7bn; after US$4.9bn net SCIP partner contributions and incentives, net capex US$11.2bn.

(17,672)"; "Proceeds from capital-related government incentives ... 1,577"; "Partner contributions, net ... 4,891"; "Net purchase of property, plant and equipment (net capital expenditures) ... (11,204)" (Q4 2025 release, non-GAAP reconciliation, twelve months)
correction: The US$4.9bn is net partner contributions only; government incentives of US$1.6bn are a separate deduction (17.7 - 1.6 - 4.9 = 11.2). Superseding claim added.

original_interpretation: Intel Foundry 2025 revenue US$17.8bn, operating loss US$10.3bn.
evidence_found: Segment results, twelve months ended Dec 27, 2025: "Revenue ... Intel Foundry ... 17,826 ... Intersegment Eliminations (17,683)"; "Operating income (loss) ... (10,318)" (Q4 2025 release, Supplemental Operating Segment Results)
notes: The release does not state the intersegment share of Foundry revenue, but company-wide intersegment eliminations of US$17.7bn against Foundry revenue of US$17.8bn are consistent with Foundry revenue being mostly internal (from Intel Products).
